scope.execution: Real Apple Silicon HVF with shared userspace Linux kernel; 12 configured CPU slots
scope.work: Four processes, 10000 resource lifecycles each; no pathname/data-file loop
scope.timing: Medians of three unprofiled repetitions; longest child loop and full workload wall time; separate profiling samples and counterbalanced version order
scope.setup: One fresh disposable pinned Alpine store per resource kind, shared by both Trames versions; import outside timed runs

operations.pipe: pipe2, write byte, read/check byte, close writer, read/check EOF, close reader
operations.eventfd: create, write/check counter, read/check counter, close
operations.timerfd: create monotonic timer, set/get disarmed state, close
operations.inotify: create nonblocking instance, read/check EAGAIN, close

scope.native: Same static ELF on existing native ARM64 Linux-kernel Lima/VZ reference, six vCPUs, 8 GiB configured; four processes. macOS fixture measures the same pipe lifecycle only.
limitations: Lifecycle microbenchmarks, not Firefox or whole-application scores.
Diagnostic samples include startup/teardown and scheduling-dependent serial tails. Counts are not deterministic admission targets.
Cohort drain time excludes dispatch/resource work and is not CPU utilization.
Native inotify reference covers empty initialization/read/close, not watch creation or directory-event throughput.
Native Linux reference was initially stopped, started after Mac timing and stopped afterward.
Unchanged interpreter/HVF CPU engines, guest-memory module and graphics code reuse prior validation; affected worker/kernel regressions were rerun.
Physical iPad testing skipped per user request; host production FFI and device cross-build passed.
